name: Design a dating application
focus: candidate retrieval, mutual-match correctness, safety, privacy, and recommendation feedback
statement: Design discovery, swipe, mutual match, messaging, and blocking for a location-aware dating product.
answer: Separate discovery ranking from authoritative swipe/match state. A match occurs only when both eligible users express the required action; enforce it atomically with idempotent writes. Candidate generation uses coarse location and preference filters, then ranking, with strict privacy controls over exact location and sensitive attributes. Blocking and unmatching must affect all read paths and caches quickly. Protect against abuse with rate limits, reporting, moderation, audit, and fair evaluation of recommendation exposure.
tests: Test simultaneous swipes, duplicate swipe, block after match, stale candidate cache, location permission withdrawal, and abusive account creation.

name: Design a real-time online auction
focus: bid ordering, atomic acceptance, anti-sniping rules, and realtime fan-out
statement: Design auctions with many concurrent bidders, visible bid updates, reserve prices, and a defined closing rule.
answer: Route each auction’s bids through one ordered authority or transactional compare-and-set so accepted bids follow a deterministic sequence. Validate bidder eligibility, amount, and auction state at acceptance time. Define tie-breaking and whether late bids extend closing time; use server time and a versioned state transition. Broadcast accepted bids asynchronously to viewers, who may see delayed updates but cannot determine the winner. Record an auditable bid log and protect against automated abuse.
tests: Test simultaneous bids, close-boundary race, duplicate client retry, stale display, auction owner update, and fan-out outage.

name: Design a multi-tenant SaaS platform
focus: tenant isolation, service tiers, metering, noisy-neighbor controls, and data lifecycle
statement: Design a SaaS platform for many organizations with different service tiers, usage billing, and tenant-specific retention or residency rules.
answer: Resolve tenant identity from a verified principal and authorize every resource access against membership. Choose silo, pool, or hybrid placement from isolation, cost, and operational requirements; enforce tenant keys in data access and tests. Apply per-tenant quotas and fair scheduling, meter billable units from auditable events, and prevent shared caches from mixing scopes. Plan tenant migration and deletion across database, object, analytics, logs, and backups. Monitor noisy-neighbor impact without unbounded metric cardinality.
tests: Test cross-tenant ID substitution, quota bypass, large tenant migration, data deletion, cache collision, and per-tier noisy neighbor.

name: Design a video-conferencing service
focus: media routing, latency budgets, signaling, recording, and network adaptation
statement: Design meetings with interactive audio/video, screen sharing, recording, and participants joining from unreliable networks.
answer: Separate control-plane signaling and room authorization from real-time media forwarding. Select peer-to-peer, selective forwarding, or mixing topology based on group size, client capabilities, bandwidth, and server cost. Route media regionally and adapt bitrate to congestion; audio usually has stricter latency needs than archival recording. Handle reconnect, mute, participant permissions, and recording consent. Monitor packet loss, jitter, round-trip time, join time, and quality by region and device.
tests: Test NAT/firewall restrictions, large meeting fan-out, region loss, bandwidth drop, participant permission change, and recording interruption.

name: Design a large-scale email service
focus: mail delivery, mailbox state, search, spam defenses, and retention
statement: Design sending and receiving email with mailbox search, attachments, threading, spam filtering, and long-term retention.
answer: Separate mail ingress/delivery from mailbox reads and search indexing. Store message metadata and bodies with durable identifiers; attachments can use deduplicated object storage with access controls. Treat delivery as asynchronous and expose queued, deferred, or bounced states. Spam and malware filters need layered signals and appeal paths. Search indexes are derived and rebuildable; define threading normalization and deletion/retention rules. Protect against address enumeration, spoofing, abuse, and cross-tenant access.
tests: Test duplicate delivery, bounce, spam false-positive appeal, attachment malware, search-index lag, and retention deletion.

name: Design live comments for a large broadcast
focus: hot-stream fan-out, moderation, batching, ordering, and slow clients
statement: Design comments for a live event with millions of viewers but far fewer commenters, including moderation and replay.
answer: Partition comment ingestion by stream and assign accepted sequence IDs. Moderate before broad fan-out where policy requires; a fast initial filter may be followed by deeper review and removal events. Batch delivery and isolate slow consumers so one connection cannot back up the stream. Persist enough for replay and moderation audit, while presence and transient reactions remain ephemeral. A single celebrity stream is a hot partition; shard fan-out and aggregate counts. Measure moderation latency, fan-out lag, drops, and reconnect recovery.
tests: Test celebrity hotspot, slow viewer, moderation reversal, duplicate comment, stream reconnect, and sudden viewer surge.

name: Design a real-time fraud detection system
focus: feature freshness, rules/model cascade, decision latency, and analyst feedback
statement: Design transaction scoring that can block or challenge suspicious activity under a strict response deadline.
answer: Define the business loss function and false-positive cost. Apply deterministic high-confidence rules first, then retrieve fresh online features and invoke a model within a bounded latency budget. Keep online/offline feature definitions aligned and versioned. A missing feature store or model should trigger a risk-specific fallback, not silently approve everything. Record decision reasons for audit and provide analyst review and appeals. Protect against feedback loops and adversarial adaptation; measure quality by cohort and latency alongside prevented loss.
tests: Test feature-store timeout, model version skew, duplicate transaction, false-positive appeal, adversarial pattern, and delayed label feedback.

name: Design a fitness tracking service
focus: GPS ingestion, activity processing, segment matching, leaderboards, and privacy
statement: Design activity recording and sharing for runners and cyclists with route maps, segment rankings, and privacy zones.
answer: Accept resumable GPS samples with device sequence and timestamps; deduplicate and validate impossible jumps. Store raw activity under user-controlled privacy and derive simplified geometry, map matching, and segment efforts asynchronously. Segment matching can use spatial prefilters followed by precise path comparison. Leaderboards are derived and need correction/rebuild when activity is edited or flagged. Hide sensitive start/end regions and enforce sharing policy in exports and cached maps. Monitor processing lag and GPS quality.
tests: Test offline upload replay, GPS drift, duplicate points, privacy-zone export, activity deletion, and leaderboard correction.

name: Design an online code-judging platform
focus: untrusted code isolation, queue fairness, deterministic testing, and contest peaks
statement: Design a coding challenge service that compiles and runs untrusted submissions and returns verdicts under bursty contest load.
answer: Store submission and problem/version metadata, then enqueue work by priority and fairness policy. Execute code only inside strongly isolated, short-lived sandboxes with CPU, memory, process, filesystem, and network limits. Treat compiler/runtime output as untrusted. Use deterministic test bundles and record toolchain versions so results can be reproduced. Separate queue admission from workers and protect contest workloads from background rejudging. Monitor queue age, sandbox resources, worker failures, and abuse.
tests: Test fork bomb, filesystem escape attempt, network access, memory exhaustion, duplicate submission, and contest queue spike.

name: Design a product price-tracking service
focus: polite data acquisition, change detection, retention, and subscriber alerts
statement: Design a service that monitors product prices over time and alerts subscribers when prices change or cross a target.
answer: Model watched URLs/products and fetch priority, enforce site terms and politeness limits, and avoid treating anti-bot evasion as the reliability plan. Normalize product identity and price with provenance and confidence. Store observations for history and detect changes with idempotent events. Queue alerts by user preference and deduplicate repeated changes. Prioritize popular watches fairly; expire invalid products. Monitor fetch success, freshness, false-change rate, and per-domain request rate.
tests: Test changed page layout, currency conversion, duplicate fetch result, stale watch, alert storm, and domain throttle.

name: Design a high-scale API gateway
focus: routing configuration, authentication boundaries, quotas, and failure isolation
statement: Design a gateway that routes many public APIs to backend services while adding authentication integration, quotas, and observability with low overhead.
answer: Keep configuration versioned and validate routes and policies before rollout. Authenticate at the edge where appropriate, but preserve backend authorization for resource-specific decisions. Apply bounded body sizes, deadlines, rate limits, and circuit behavior; avoid automatically retrying unsafe requests. Separate control plane from request data plane and support staged propagation/rollback. Redundancy and dependency behavior must avoid a gateway becoming a universal outage. Track per-route latency and errors with bounded labels.
tests: Test malformed config rollout, auth provider outage, retry duplication, large request body, route explosion, and control-plane partition.

name: Design a CI/CD platform
focus: workflow scheduling, ephemeral runners, artifact integrity, secrets, and tenant isolation
statement: Design a hosted build platform that executes customer workflows with caches, artifacts, secrets, and concurrent jobs.
answer: Parse workflow definitions into a validated DAG and schedule jobs with fair tenant quotas. Execute untrusted build code on isolated ephemeral runners; scope credentials to the minimum step and never expose secrets to untrusted fork workflows. Store artifacts by immutable digest with provenance and access policy. Cache keys include relevant inputs and tenant boundaries. Cancellation and retries must not duplicate release side effects. Observe queue wait, runner saturation, cache hits, artifact integrity, and secret-access audit.
tests: Test malicious workflow, forked pull request, runner reuse leak, cache poisoning, artifact substitution, and cancellation during publish.

name: Design an observability platform
focus: multi-signal ingestion, cardinality, trace correlation, query isolation, and retention
statement: Design ingestion and query for metrics, logs, and traces across many hosts and multiple customer organizations.
answer: Define signal contracts and ingestion priorities with backpressure. Enforce tenant isolation and cardinality budgets at ingestion; reject or transform unbounded metric dimensions deliberately. Store hot queryable data separately from archive and preserve trace/log correlation. Sampling and aggregation reduce cost but change what can be investigated, so document policy and retain aggregate SLO metrics. Isolate expensive queries from ingestion and alert evaluation. Measure dropped telemetry, ingest lag, query tails, and cost per tenant.
tests: Test telemetry flood, cardinality spike, tenant query isolation, collector outage, sampling-induced missing trace, and retention policy.

name: Design a web-scale search engine
focus: crawl/index pipelines, inverted indexes, ranking, freshness, and query serving
statement: Design search over a large document corpus with ranked results, low query latency, and frequent content updates.
answer: Separate crawling, parsing, deduplication, indexing, and query serving. Build sharded inverted indexes and support incremental updates while retaining a consistent index generation. Query fan-out gathers shard results, merges scores, and applies reranking within latency budget. Ranking combines lexical relevance, freshness, quality, and policy; evaluate offline and online. Cache common queries carefully and protect against abuse. Monitor index freshness, shard tail latency, zero-result rate, and ranking quality by cohort.
tests: Test shard loss, duplicate/canonical URLs, stale deleted page, adversarial SEO, rare query, and index rebuild.

name: Design a retail brokerage platform
focus: order lifecycle, market-data fan-out, ledger/tax lots, and auditability
statement: Design trading for retail users with order submission, streaming quotes, portfolio views, fractional shares, and regulatory records.
answer: Separate market-data distribution from order authority. Validate eligibility, buying power, and order parameters before accepting an order with a stable ID and state machine. Route execution to providers and reconcile fills, cancels, and partial outcomes. Portfolio and tax-lot projections are derived but must reconcile to authoritative transactions. Quote fan-out is high volume and time-sensitive; label freshness and avoid presenting stale values as executable prices. Retain auditable records and tightly control financial data.
tests: Test duplicate order submit, partial fill, cancel/fill race, stale quote, reconciliation mismatch, and provider outage.

name: Design channel-scale team chat
focus: large-room fan-out, workspace authorization, presence aggregation, and search
statement: Design team chat with channels that may have very large membership, threads, presence, file sharing, and workspace search.
answer: Use workspace/channel membership as an authoritative authorization boundary and check before delivery and search results. Persist messages with channel-scoped ordering; separate presence from durable content. For large channels, shard fan-out and batch updates rather than synchronously delivering to every member. Search is a derived index that must respect current membership and deletion. Thread replies and reactions have distinct query patterns. Measure hot spots, delivery lag, presence freshness, and search access filtering.
tests: Test member removal during delivery, a very large channel, duplicate message, presence storm, deleted message in search, and workspace boundary leakage.
